I'm not talking graphic design here - we all know how important iconography and clear, easy to understand design is. I'm talking straight up art. Would Abyss be the game it was if the artwork weren't as good? Would other games feel better if they had better art, even though the mechanics were the same?
How important is the artwork in games you play?

There's a lot of wiggle room when talking about art in a game because it's often so closely tied to the theme. Art plays a huge part in initial appeal and getting someone to play your game in the first place is often the hardest part of selling a game.

The breath of creature was warm and rancid. It stung his eyes through the visor, causing small tears to form. No one had made it this far, through the cave where the beast resided. Was he brave enough to defeat it? Had he done the right thing? Was she worth it? Now was not a time for questions and self doubt. Now was a time for action and bravery. He raised the shield she had given him for the journey. The sweat was forming and dripped down in waves over the back of his neck.The sword ached in his hand, it was heavy but needed. His eyes narrowed, the beast breathed in deep. Their stand off was about to end. He ran forward.

He awoke from the dream. Sweat everywhere. He looked over at his wife. She was asleep. He knew he had to fight for her. Now was a time for action.
